explanation: The rule says 'nine known' control types but the code (AdmlFile.vb 49-105) knows eight: text, decimalTextBox, textBox, checkBox, comboBox, dropdownList, listBox, multiTextBox, which is the list the rule itself gives. Fix the count. Also say that a recognised control with no refId is still shown, it simply is not tied to a policy input.

Each step is taken only if the ADML file actually exists in that folder, not merely when the folder exists. An exact-language folder without the file falls through to the sibling-language search, then to en-US. A same-language sibling is chosen only if it holds the file; the first such folder in listing order wins. State that existence of the file, not of the folder, decides each step.

A list element without a valuePrefix (or with an empty one) also takes its registry value name from the element's valueName, because the fallback at line 250 applies whenever the value name is still empty. The rule says valueName applies to 'other elements' only. Restate: the prefix wins when non-empty; otherwise valueName is used, for every element type. HasPrefix is true whenever the attribute is present, even if empty.

says: Load-time linking can abort the whole load, which no rule states. BuildStructures runs outside AddSingleAdmx's try blocks. A policy with no parentCategory or no supportedOn element is accepted by AdmxFile.Load (the CategoryID/SupportedCode stay empty) but ResolveRef then fails on an empty reference. A category element with child nodes but no parentCategory child fails in AdmxFile.Load, so it is reported as an invalid ADMX. Two categories, products, support rules or policies with the same name in one ADMX collide on the per-load dictionary and fail the linking. A target namespace missing from policyNamespaces leaves the namespace empty, and the namespace check throws unguarded. Write rule(s) for what a person sees (the load stops with an error rather than skipping the file) or an assumption where the code leaves the outcome to an unhandled exception.

Rule on the ADML string/presentation duplicates and required attributes omits that a string or presentation element without an id is also refused (the id attribute is read unguarded), and that a presentation's refId-less controls are kept. Add the missing-id clause to the ADML validity rule.
